links.comparator_used: Original brain MRI reports in native format without lay summary
links.outcome: Objective comprehension (correct classification of whether report explains headache); also satisfaction, subjective comprehension, anxiety
links.effect: Objective comprehension 58.3% vs 59.4% (OR 0.97; 95% CI 0.90–1.06; P = .54); satisfaction 64.9% vs 36.7% (OR 3.26); subjective comprehension 50.3% vs 24.0% (OR 3.17); high anxiety 25.1% vs 26.6% (OR 0.92; P = .037); symptom-explaining reports 42.4% vs 37.4%; normal reports 72.5% vs 76.6%
links.tradeoff: Gap between perceived and actual understanding; reduced objective comprehension for normal reports (72.5% vs 76.6%, P = .001)
links.quote: LLM-generated lay summaries appended to brain MRI reports improved patient satisfaction and subjective comprehension but did not improve objective comprehension, indicating a gap between perceived and actual understanding that should be addressed before clinical integration.

design_hint: appending LLM-generated lay summaries to radiology reports for patients
